objective: Turn one released organizational claim into one durable domain-local execution attempt whose exact HOW/runtime/outcome can be reconstructed, without moving organizational scheduling into the strategy/runtime.
architectureDecisions: organization/lifecycle chooses WHAT and ownership; DOMAIN_EXECUTION_CONTROL owns HOW only after released claim
ExecutionPolicy is immutable/versioned with a CAS-fenced current head
ExecutionAttemptHead is read before any policy resolution; ACTIVE/RECOVERY_REQUIRED reuses the existing immutable binding
ExecutionAttemptBinding pins exact WorkContract, release receipt, policy, strategy, runtime/config/context refs before effects
semantic executionAttemptId is distinct from runtime invocation id
strategy result is not runtime fact, runtime fact is not verification evidence, and execution success is not domain acceptance
domain acceptance is distinct from authoritative domain publication
Restate may be an adapter/runtime but is not organization workflow authority
strategy cannot dispatch authoritative work into another domain

implementationSlices.output: ExecutionPolicy/ExecutionStrategyDescriptor immutable artifacts plus trusted policy publisher and CAS current head
requirements: policy keyed by domain + workloadType with explicit WorkContract compatibility
policy/strategy cannot rewrite work inputs, outputs, acceptance, owner, priority or downstream obligations
policy head race before first binding forces re-resolution; promotion after binding affects new attempts only
ABSENT may resolve policy/strategy and CAS-create first semantic attempt
ACTIVE/RECOVERY_REQUIRED loads existing binding before policy resolution
stable attempt-scoped runtime invocation/idempotency identity is fixed before dispatch where runtime supports it

implementationSlices.output: one concrete BA-owned execution strategy adapter using existing Core/runtime primitives
requirements: same WorkContract and acceptance semantics under any strategy
no Backend->QA or other cross-domain dispatch
Restate is optional for this slice; contract must not depend on Restate to be correct
RuntimeExecutionAttestation comes from trusted adapter/platform boundary rather than strategy self-report
ExecutionAttemptOutcome preserves candidate outputs, effects, counterevidence and proposed derivation edges
DomainPublicationReceipt is the authoritative write/publication boundary and publishes accepted derivation edges
ExecutionJudgmentBundle is derived orientation only and re-resolves source refs

implementationSlices.output: worktree projection + deterministic BA fixture + crash/race regression suite
requirements: raw strategy lineage is never authoritative dependency truth

hardInvariants: policy promotion never rewrites an in-flight binding
process restart alone cannot mint a new semantic execution attempt
acceptanceCriteria: one released BA-owned work item executes through DomainExecutionController and leaves a complete reconstructable binding->runtime->outcome->decision->publication chain
same active/recovery attempt survives process restart without re-resolving newer policy/strategy
policy head race before binding fails/re-resolves; policy promotion after binding does not change the attempt
runtime code/deployment identity is exact and trusted, not mutable latest/self-report
claim/release authority is revalidated immediately before first runtime/effect dispatch
human-assisted or alternate strategy cannot bypass completion/publication gates
fresh process can resolve all correctness-relevant refs and distinguish historical validity from authority needed for a new mutation
mandatoryNegativeTests: Backend strategy dispatches QA organizational work
strategy self-reports runtime version without trusted attestation
process restart creates second semantic attempt
raw proposed lineage becomes cross-domain dependency truth
mutable latest runtime alias satisfies exact runtime identity
forbidden: global StrategyRegistry unless a concrete second consumer proves it is required

activation.baselinePolicy: Retained delivery spec only; this artifact does not reactivate terminal work.
